Semaglutide trial reports 20% lower cardiovascular risk

A large randomized study extends the conversation beyond weight loss, examining heart attack, stroke and cardiovascular death.

Field Notes demo desk · Historical scenario: November 11, 2023

Semaglutide reduced the risk of major cardiovascular events by 20% in a 2023 randomized trial involving people with overweight or obesity and established cardiovascular disease. The result puts a possible heart benefit alongside the drug’s better-known effects on body weight.

The finding comes from a study published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Participants received once-weekly semaglutide or placebo, and researchers tracked a combined outcome of cardiovascular death, nonfatal heart attack or nonfatal stroke.

The trial enrolled adults aged 45 or older who did not have diabetes. Its results add evidence about a particular group of patients; they do not establish the same benefit for every person considering a weight-loss medicine.

The report also describes adverse events and treatment discontinuations. Those details matter when considering how an overall trial result might translate into a treatment decision. The study’s full record is linked above for readers who want to examine the evidence behind the headline.
